newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala 9-month trade deficit down 23 percent.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala 9-month trade deficit down 23 percent.

text.p: Guatemala's trade deficit for the first three quarters of 1996 was $726 million, down 23 percent from the same period last year, Central Bank President Willy Zapata said Thursday.
The deficit for the same period in 1995 was $944 million, Zapata told a news conference.
Zapata said a 32 percent increase in the value of non-traditional exports so far this year is largely responsible for an increase in export income and the lower deficit.

The value of cloth and thread exports during the first three quarters of this year increased by 64 percent over the same period in 1995. Cotton and cotton derivatives showed an increase of 176 percent. Honey and minerals both showed increases of over 200 percent.
The total value of exports rose only 2.3 percent, to $1.58 billion, in the first nine months of 1996 from $1.54 billion in the same period this year.
Zapata blamed international prices for the decreased value of most of Guatemala's traditional exports such as sugar, coffee and meat.
Comparing the first three quarters of 1995 and 1996, export volumes have not decreased for bananas, coffee, sugar or petroleum.
The value of coffee exports was off 17.3 percent despite a 23.6 percent increase in volume exported through September 1996, he said.
A slowdown in Guatemala's economic growth has slowed imports, which also affected the trade balance, Zapata said.

In the first nine months of the year, total imports were $2.31 billion compared to $2.49 billion in the same period in 1995. While imports of combustibles and construction materials increased, there was an 11.3 percent drop in imports of consumer goods and a 9.7 percent drop in imports of raw materials for industry and agriculture.
